parameter.name: canonicalize_user_services
parameter.description:
A comma-separated list of PAM service names for which the PAM module replaces .B PAM_USER with the canonical account name after a successful authentication. The canonical account name is the name the system name service returns for the authenticated account, which is also the name reported by .B id -un for that user.
Users can log in with several aliases of the same account, such as the UPN, the short name, or a different letter case. Some applications, such as GDM, copy .B PAM_USER into the .B USER and .B LOGNAME environment variables of the session, which then contain the alias entered at the login prompt instead of the account name.
The PAM service name is the name passed by the application when calling .B pam_start() (e.g., "gdm-password", "login").
Entries are matched as substrings, so "gdm" will match "gdm-password", "gdm-autologin", etc.
.B PAM_USER is only replaced when the canonical account name resolves to the same account as the name entered at the login prompt. Do not list sshd: it requires .B PAM_USER to remain unchanged during authentication, and already sets .B USER and .B LOGNAME from the account name.
By default, no service is listed and .B PAM_USER is never modified.
parameter.conf_description: PAM services whose PAM_USER is set to the canonical account name.
